summary: Dependency-confusion beacon POSTs host identifiers to hardcoded bare-IP endpoint at install and import
details: The package self-describes as a 'Compatibility shim' and ships a Proxy-based index.js whose only runtime effect is to return no-op functions for any property access, allowing builds that resolve this name to complete without errors. In parallel, beacon.cjs runs from the postinstall lifecycle hook and is also invoked when index.js is required, POSTing host identifiers (os.hostname(), __dirname, process.cwd(), process.version) over plain HTTP to the hardcoded bare-IP endpoint http://185.158.107.175:8787/_ah/dc. The combination of a hollow Proxy shim, a name under a vendor-looking scope, and an install- and import-time beacon to an unrelated bare-IP collector is the fingerprint of a dependency-confusion / name-squat probe: installers that mistakenly resolve this package name silently complete their builds while leaking host and path identifiers to an attacker-controlled endpoint.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
